data.name: AppName
data.comment: The product's name, as message box titles show it. Usually left as it is.

data.name: Tooltip
data.comment: Shown when the pointer rests on the tray icon. {0} is the status line, such as "example-landscape · 30 fps · Universal Screen 8.8". Windows cuts it at 127 characters.

data.name: StatusShowing
data.comment: The menu's first line while a theme is on the screen. {0} is the theme's name, {1:0} the frames per second it reaches, {2} the screen's name.

data.name: StatusPaused
data.value: Paused: the screen is free for other programs
data.comment: The menu's first line after Pause.

data.name: StatusWaitingForScreen
data.comment: The menu's first line when no screen is plugged in, or another program has it. Marquee takes it as soon as it can.

data.name: StatusThemeFailed
data.value: Not showing: the theme didn't load
data.comment: The menu's first line when the theme had an error at start; the error is on the next line.

data.name: StatusNoTheme
data.comment: The menu's first line when config.yaml names a theme that can't be found; the reason is on the next line.

data.name: StatusLConnectBusy
data.comment: The menu's first line while L-Connect 3's background service holds the screen. "L-Connect" stays as it is.

data.name: StatusDownloading
data.comment: The menu's first line while an update downloads. {0} is the new version, {1} how much of it has arrived, as a whole percentage.

data.name: StatusInstalling
data.comment: The menu's first line while the installer of an update runs; the screen is paused meanwhile. {0} is the new version.

data.name: MenuThemes
data.comment: The submenu listing the themes to pick from: the user's own, then the installed examples.

data.name: MenuNoThemes
data.comment: The Themes submenu's only line when no theme folder holds a theme.

data.name: MenuOrientation
data.comment: The submenu for how the screen is mounted.

data.name: OrientationLandscape
data.comment: The screen mounted wide, the way it ships.

data.name: OrientationLandscapeFlipped
data.comment: The screen mounted wide and turned over.

data.name: OrientationPortrait
data.comment: The screen mounted tall.

data.name: OrientationPortraitFlipped
data.comment: The screen mounted tall and turned over.

data.name: MenuOpenPreview
data.comment: Opens a window showing what the screen shows.

data.name: MenuOpenThemesFolder
data.comment: Opens the folder where the user's own themes go, in File Explorer.

data.name: MenuOpenLogs
data.comment: Opens the folder of Marquee's daily log files, in File Explorer.

data.name: MenuEditTheme
data.comment: Opens the theme editor on the theme on the screen.

data.name: MenuEditSettings
data.comment: Opens config.yaml in the user's editor for .yaml files.

data.name: MenuPause
data.comment: Stops showing and lets go of the screen, so another program can use it.

data.name: MenuResume
data.comment: Shows the theme again after Pause.

data.name: MenuTakeOver
data.value: Take over the screen from L-Connect
data.comment: A menu item while L-Connect 3's background service holds the screen: Marquee stops the service, opens the screen and starts the service again. "L-Connect" stays as it is.

data.name: MenuAlwaysTakeOver
data.comment: A checkable menu item: checked, Marquee takes the screen from L-Connect by itself (lconnect.handover: auto in config.yaml); unchecked, it asks first (ask).

data.name: TakeOverNeedsAdministrator
data.value: Marquee can take the screen from L-Connect only when it runs as administrator, as its logon task starts it.
data.comment: A line in the menu while L-Connect holds the screen and the tray isn't elevated (started by hand, or by a user who isn't an administrator).

data.name: TakeOverTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon that offers to take the screen from L-Connect (lconnect.handover: ask).

data.name: TakeOverPrompt
data.value: Marquee can take it over while L-Connect keeps running your fans and RGB. Click here to take over.
data.comment: The text of the balloon that offers to take the screen from L-Connect; clicking the balloon does it. "RGB" means the PC's colored lights.

data.name: FirstRunTakeOverPrompt
data.value: {0} To do this at every start, choose "{1}" in Marquee's menu.
data.comment: The text of the balloon that offers, once, to take the screen from L-Connect to a user who hasn't chosen what Marquee does when L-Connect holds the screen. {0} is TakeOverPrompt; {1} is the menu item MenuAlwaysTakeOver.

data.name: HandoverFailedTitle
data.value: Couldn't take the screen from L-Connect
data.comment: The title of the balloon shown when taking the screen from L-Connect failed; the text says why.

data.name: HandoverFailed
data.comment: The text of the balloon shown when taking the screen from L-Connect failed. {0} is what went wrong, a sentence or two in English.

data.name: HandoverFailedRetrying
data.value: {0} Marquee will keep trying. See the log for details.
data.comment: The text of the balloon shown when taking the screen from L-Connect failed and lconnect.handover is auto, so Marquee tries again by itself (after 1 minute, then 2, 5, then every 10). {0} is what went wrong, a sentence or two in English.

data.name: HandoverFailedProblem
data.value: Couldn't take the screen from L-Connect: {0}
data.comment: A line in the menu after taking the screen from L-Connect failed, until Marquee gets the screen. {0} is what went wrong, a sentence or two in English. "L-Connect" stays as it is.

data.name: MenuCheckForUpdates
data.comment: A menu item that looks for a newer Marquee on GitHub now.

data.name: MenuInstallUpdate
data.comment: A menu item once a newer Marquee is found: downloads it, checks its signature and installs it. {0} is its version.

data.name: MenuDownloadUpdate
data.comment: The same item when Marquee isn't running as administrator and can't install: it opens the new version's page in the browser. {0} is its version.

data.name: UpdateAvailableTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon that says a newer Marquee is out.

data.name: UpdateAvailable
data.value: Marquee {0} is available. Click to install.
data.comment: The text of that balloon; clicking it downloads and installs the update. {0} is the new version.

data.name: UpdateAvailableDownload
data.value: Marquee {0} is available. Click to open its download page.
data.comment: The text of that balloon when Marquee isn't running as administrator: clicking it opens the new version's page in the browser. {0} is the new version.

data.name: UpToDateTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon after "Check for updates" found nothing newer.

data.name: UpToDate
data.comment: The text of that balloon. {0} is the running version.

data.name: UpdateCheckFailedTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon when "Check for updates" got no answer it could use; the text says why, in English.

data.name: UpdateFailedTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon when an update couldn't be downloaded, verified or started; the text says why, in English. Marquee keeps running.

data.name: UpdateFailed
data.comment: Logged when the folder updates are downloaded into can't be used. {0} is the reason.

data.name: UpdateDidNotInstall
data.comment: The balloon's text, and the log line, when the installer of an update ended without installing it (the user cancelled it, another installation was under way, it failed); Marquee carries on as before. {0} is the installer's exit code, {1} the full path of its log file.

data.name: InstallerFinishedWithoutQuit
data.value: The installer finished (code {0}) without closing Marquee, so there was nothing to update; Marquee carries on.
data.comment: Logged when the installer of an update ended successfully but never asked the tray to quit. {0} is its exit code.

data.name: UpdateTimerFailed
data.value: The daily update check failed unexpectedly: {0}
data.comment: Logged when the timer for the daily update check hits an error it didn't expect; it carries on. {0} is the reason.

data.name: NoReleaseKeyTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon after "Check for updates" in a build that has no release key to check updates with (a development build).

data.name: NoReleaseKey
data.value: Download new versions from {0}. Click here to open it.
data.comment: The text of that balloon; clicking it opens the page. {0} is the address of Marquee's releases on GitHub.

data.name: MenuAbout
data.comment: Shows the version and license.

data.name: MenuQuit
data.comment: Stops Marquee and removes the tray icon until the next logon.

data.name: About
data.comment: The About box's text. {0} is the version, such as 0.1.0. Lian Li and Universal Screen are product names.

data.name: FirstRunHintTitle
data.value: Marquee is showing an example theme
data.comment: The title of the balloon shown once, on the first start.

data.name: FirstRunHint
data.value: Pick your theme and the screen's orientation from Marquee's menu: click its icon here.
data.comment: The balloon shown once, on the first start, pointing at the tray icon's menu.

data.name: ThemeFailedTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon that shows a theme's error, with its file and line.

data.name: ThemeProblem
data.comment: A line in the menu under the status. {0} is the error, in English, starting with its file and line.

data.name: ConfigFailedTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon shown when config.yaml can't be used. config.yaml is a file name.

data.name: ConfigInvalid
data.value: config.yaml has an error, so Marquee uses the default settings: {0}
data.comment: Logged and shown in the menu at start. {0} is the error, in English, starting with its line number where there is one.

data.name: ConfigUnreadable
data.value: config.yaml can't be read, so Marquee uses the default settings: {0}
data.comment: Logged and shown in the menu at start. {0} is Windows' reason.

data.name: ConfigChangeInvalid
data.value: {0} (the current settings stay until config.yaml is fixed)
data.comment: Logged and shown when config.yaml changes while Marquee runs but can't be used. {0} is the error, starting with its line number where there is one.

data.name: FpsNeedsAdministrator
data.value: Game FPS is off: Marquee isn't running as administrator.
data.comment: A line in the menu when the FPS provider is on but the tray isn't elevated (started by hand, or by a user who isn't an administrator).

data.name: ConfigNotWatched
data.value: Marquee can't watch config.yaml for changes, so edits apply at the next start: {0}
data.comment: Logged when the folder config.yaml goes in can't be made. {0} is Windows' reason.

data.name: ScreenRetryFailed
data.comment: Logged when the timed retry for a screen that wasn't there fails unexpectedly. {0} is the reason.

data.name: ScreenMarkerFailed
data.value: Marquee couldn't mark the screen as the tray's, so marquee run won't say that the tray has it: {0}
data.comment: Logged when the named object that tells marquee run the tray has the screen can't be made. {0} is the reason. "marquee run" stays as it is.

data.name: CommandFailedTitle
data.comment: The title of the balloon shown when a menu command fails; the text says why.

data.name: CommandFailed
data.comment: Logged when a menu command fails. {0} is the reason.

data.name: NoDesktopShell
data.value: Explorer, the Windows desktop, isn't running, so Marquee opened nothing: without it, what the tray opens would run as administrator. Try again once the taskbar is back.
data.comment: The balloon text when a menu item that opens a folder, a file or a web page is clicked while Explorer, the Windows desktop shell, isn't running (after it crashed, say).

data.name: EditorMissing
data.value: The theme editor isn't installed beside the tray: there is no {0}. Reinstall Marquee to get it back.
data.comment: The balloon text when Edit theme is clicked and the theme editor isn't there. {0} is the full path of MarqueeEditor.exe where it looked.

data.name: PreviewStatus
data.value: {0:0.0} fps (target {1}) · render {2:0.0} ms · send {3:0.0} ms · {4} frames sent
data.comment: Shown each second in the preview opened from the tray. {0:0.0} is the frame rate, {1} the target rate, {2:0.0} and {3:0.0} milliseconds per frame to render and to send, {4} the frames sent so far.

data.name: DataFolderUnusable
data.value: Marquee is running as administrator, so it keeps its log and the Claude Code limits in a folder only administrators can change, and that folder can't be used. {0}
data.comment: A message box when the tray, elevated, can't use its folder under %ProgramData%\Marquee, and stops. {0} says which folder and why, and what to do, in English.

data.name: TrayStarted
data.comment: The log's first line from the tray. {0} is the version.

data.name: TrayStopped
data.comment: The log's last line from the tray, after Quit.

data.name: WindowsResumed
data.value: Windows resumed from sleep; reopening the screen.
data.comment: Logged when Windows wakes from sleep and the tray reopens the screen.

data.name: QuitEventTaken
data.value: Another program made the event the installer uses to close Marquee's tray ({0}) first, so the tray won't listen for it: an install or uninstall will end the tray instead, without saving its state.
data.comment: Logged at start when the tray's quit event already exists. {0} is the event's name. Usually a tray that is still exiting; restarting the tray makes the event again.
